The core derivation begins with two players forming noisy probabilities P_B, P_S ∼ U(L, H), where L = P_T − ε·min(1−P_T, P_T), H = P_T + ε·min(1−P_T, P_T). The consensus P_C = (P_B + P_S)/2. Zero-expectation fairness requires π̄_{So} = 0, which leads to a system of equations defining the noise wedge m. This m adjusts the reciprocal odds 1/P_C to account for belief dispersion. When P_C > 0.5, m is subtracted from P_C; when P_C < 0.5, m is added. The resulting odds 1/(P_C ± m) reflect structural bias correction. The failure mode occurs when ε → 0 (no noise) or when P_C → 0 or 1 (boundary instability).
